solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Blimey! Free gold in passage

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
to free is to rid
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the gold they have found lying loose in a passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A corridor is a long passage inside a building, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Medical instrument books getting zero room

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
the figure zero looks like the letter O
scope means room or space to act

explanation.surface: A medical device needs books and leaves no space for anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the instrument a doctor uses to look inside the ear.

clue.text: Confidence boosters scare as nurse gets jittery

indicators.note: jittery means nervous and shaking, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous nurse frightens a patient instead of calming them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word; 'jittery' shuffles SCARE AS NURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of reassurance raise someone's confidence, so they are confidence boosters.

clue.text: Doctor working with energy is an idiot

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: A hard-working, energetic doctor is still called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: DRONGO is Australian slang for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Drongo is Australian slang for a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed, love to try again

parts.note: an embarrassed face goes red
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A blushing suitor works up the nerve to try once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to do it over, giving it another attempt.

clue.text: Call one group up, finding bugs

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: Someone phones a group to report finding insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are wood-eating insects, and bugs is a loose word for insects.

clue.text: Tree (English) in flames

parts.note: a fir is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: An English tree is burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is the burning that shows itself as flames, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: One willing to try a right-winger getting cut short

parts.note: to test is to try

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, a right-winger

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to give a right-wing politician a go, though his speech is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One willing' is a pun: a testator is someone making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so the clue treats them as one willing.

clue.text: Work out tax

definitions.meaning: to work out at a gym
to tax a mind or muscle is to ... or test it

explanation.definitionFit: Exercise means both a workout and making demands on, or taxing, a faculty.

clue.text: Couch in terms of antitheses

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something is phrased as a set of opposites.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across termS OF Antitheses.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch and a sofa are the same piece of seating furniture.

clue.text: No more men? It's bad, but temporary lapse

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled and need rearranging

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe gives no letter

explanation.surface: Someone laments a world without men, then admits it was only a passing slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges NO MORE MEN ITS; 'but' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior moment is a brief memory lapse jokingly blamed on age.

clue.text: Before journey, miss the first course

indicators.note: before tells us the next piece comes ahead of the word for journey

parts.note: an unmarried girl, or miss, is a maiden
a voyage is a journey

explanation.surface: Before setting out, someone skips the starter at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage is a ship's first trip, its first course across the sea.

clue.text: A cop duo's excited by TV series

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters of a, cop, duo and s taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of police officers get thrilled by a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A docusoap is a documentary series following real people like a soap opera.

clue.text: Advertises connections to the national grid

definitions.meaning: to plug a product is to promote it
electric ... connect appliances to the mains supply

explanation.definitionFit: Plugs means both promotes and the electrical fittings that connect to the mains.

clue.text: Room available for hire, accommodating one

indicators.note: accommodating means housing something, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a property to let is available for rent
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A rental room is advertised that will house one person.
explanation.definitionFit: A toilet is a room containing a lavatory, as in a bathroom.

clue.text: Bride lost heart, getting thank you letter from abroad

indicators.note: lost heart means the middle letters of the word go missing

parts.note: the inner letters of the word bride
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A bride, dejected, receives a thank-you letter from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign letter.

clue.text: Little brother feels pain and opens up

parts.note: bro is a shortened form of brother
one who aches feels pain

explanation.surface: A small sibling is hurting and finally confides.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to open it up for discussion.

clue.text: Ship with cargo of sweet potatoes

indicators.note: a ship with a cargo holds something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
pud, short for pudding, is a British word for a dessert or sweet

explanation.surface: A vessel is loaded with sweet potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spuds is informal British slang for potatoes.

clue.text: Cutting remarks finishing trial

indicators.note: finishing points to the letter that ends the word

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial

explanation.surface: Sharp comments bring a court case to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing is cutting, as in shearing wool from sheep.

clue.text: Regularly leave euro? Always

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a country should quit the single currency for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of LEAVE EURO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always, as in ever hopeful.

clue.text: Island adopted by strangely intense scientist

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so one piece is placed inside the other
strangely means the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A peculiar, intense scientist takes on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges INTENSE to EINSTEN, and 'adopted by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein is the famous physicist behind relativity.

clue.text: One who sees vehicle reversing, surrounded by Spanish cheer

indicators.note: surrounded by means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: ole is the Spanish shout of approval

indicators.note: reversing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A Spanish crowd cheers a car backing up, watched by an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a seer, someone who sees the future.

clue.text: Postponing visit, initially in broken English

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the other
broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled
initially points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone puts off a trip, explaining in halting English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ENGLISH to SHELING, and 'in' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelving a plan means putting it aside for later, postponing it.

clue.text: Ran away, leaving returning bride poleaxed

indicators.note: returning means the letters are read backwards
leaving points to letters left within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone flees, leaving a bride stunned at the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: The run briDE POLEaxed, read backwards, gives the answer; 'returning' does the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry.

clue.text: Carry votes on troubled extension to home

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A council vote on a home extension is fraught.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatory is a glass room built on as an extension to a house.

clue.text: Daring to kiss

definitions.meaning: British informal use: cheek or impudence, nerve

explanation.definitionFit: Neck means brazen nerve, and as a verb means to kiss and cuddle.

clue.text: A Geordie wife — not for the first time!

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in north-east England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A Newcastle woman insists she has done this before.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means again, so something done anew is not being done for the first time.

clue.text: Times chasing copy from summit

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the next

parts.note: to ape is to copy
the multiplication sign looks like an X

explanation.surface: A newspaper pursues a copy of a summit report.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the very top or summit.

clue.text: Cash given to former telecommunications facility

parts.note: ex means former
change is cash in coins

explanation.surface: Money is handed to an ex-partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link word placing the cash after the former.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone exchange is the facility that connects calls.

clue.text: New dog is trained to get ducks

indicators.note: trained means made to behave differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new dog is trained to retrieve ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is part of the fodder, not the indicator; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Widgeons are a kind of wild duck.
